per_pair.why: Game B's dungeon architecture is more clearly defined and readable with better spatial clarity.
Game A's sandy arena is washed out and flat; Game B's dark dungeon with glowing light is dramatically superior.
Both show good light sources, but Game B's is cleaner, more refined, and better integrated.
Game A's motion strip shows jarring palette shifts across areas; Game B maintains consistent visual identity throughout.

loser_biggest_gap: Game A lacks a unified visual identity—it jumps between distinct color palettes (purple dungeon, tan desert, red areas) that feel disconnected. The sandy environment in particular is too bright and washed out, losing depth and polish.
loser_other_gaps: Lighting in bright areas needs stronger shadow and depth to match the polish of Game B's darker scenes
Environmental architectural detail and consistency needs to be refined across all areas
Overall color harmony and cohesion—pick a core palette and commit to it
reasoning: Game B demonstrates the hallmarks of a finished, beautiful indie game: consistent visual identity, expert lighting that integrates atmosphere with readability, pixel-perfect clarity, and strong artistic direction. Every scene maintains a cohesive dark-dungeon aesthetic with warm golden torchlight that creates both mood and functional lighting. Game A has atmospheric moments but fragmented aesthetics and a washed-out sandy zone that significantly undermine its polish and professionalism.
